title: Clenshaw Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Spatial GCN models face degradation problems including over-smoothing and gradient vanishing.

gap.claim: Current residual connections do not effectively harness the full potential of polynomial filters commonly used in spectral-domain GNNs.

narrative_sequence.summary: GCNs use stacked message-passing convolution layers and are foundational spatial methods for graph representation learning.
Polynomial filters are motivated from a spectral perspective and offer advantages on heterophilous graphs.
Recent spatial GCNs use residual connections to mitigate over-smoothing and gradient vanishing.
Existing residual connections do not fully exploit polynomial filters used in spectral-domain GNNs.
